A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACRec research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Pages 2–15 are textually and visually identical; page 1 differs only in the title and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments in Tables 4–5, validation experiments in Appendix B, and manual evaluations of generated statements in Section 4.2 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original recommendation experiments, appendix validation results, and manual evaluations of generated statements.

M1.justification: The ACRec architecture, text embeddings, short- and long-term preference modeling, cosine feature, and Bayesian personalized ranking objective are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Goodreads-derived book-recommendation dataset and the same full-description and affective-only evaluation populations. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each experiment: Table 4 retains SASRec, BERT4Rec, UniSRec, and RecFormer; Table 5 additionally retains LLaRA, iLoRA, and their AC variants. Appendix B retains the same validation comparators.

E3.justification: The chronological splits, sampling procedures, model settings, metrics, all-item evaluation, and 20-item evaluation are unchanged, as are the appendix validation protocols.

E4.justification: The input-content comparison, layer and cosine-feature analyses, short-term history sensitivity analysis in Tables 6–7, and Section 5 error analysis are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including ACRec's 15.6% HR@10 in Table 4 and 67.6% Top-1 accuracy in Table 5 with A + AC + C input. Appendix results and emotion-category counts are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, long-term weighting formula, recommendation-score equations, and training objective in Section 3 and Appendix B are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same task, dataset, method, and effectiveness claims. The new title emphasizes text-based recommendations and explicit affective preferences already central to v1.

C2.justification: The retrospective-evaluation caveat, interpretations of affective versus cognitive inputs, error explanations, and limitations concerning domain coverage and cold-start users are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation, embedding, prompt, hyperparameter, hardware, and runtime disclosures remain identical, including Appendices A–E. The prompt-repository access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and references are identical, including positioning relative to affective, conversational, and beyond-accuracy recommender systems.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Leveraging Descriptions of Emotional Preferences in Recommender Systems' to 'A Text-Based Recommender System that Leverages Explicit Affective State Preferences'. The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; body wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2, Tables 1–8, captions, placement, and page layout are unchanged. The revised title retains the same two-line format, and pages 2–15 render identically.

improvement.justification: The revision only changes the title and arXiv stamp. Although the title states the existing approach more explicitly, the scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations remain identical, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
